newsitem.title: CUBA: Despite embargo, regatta brings U.S. boats to Cuba.
newsitem.headline: Despite embargo, regatta brings U.S. boats to Cuba.

text.p: About 70 small boats carrying U.S. citizens tied up at the Hemingway Marina on Sunday as part of a Tampa-to-Havana regatta, an event that was held annually prior to the 1959 Cuban revolution.

Some 50 or 60 boats with U.S crews and passengers are expected to join those already here on Monday and Tuesday. At least 500 Americans are expected to reach Havana over the next few days, the greatest influx of U.S citizens for a single event since the Pan Amercian Games in 1991.

U.S citizens are subject to stiff penalties for violating the Trading with the Enemy Act, which prohibits them from spending money in Cuba. But Washington gave permission to the regatta participants as long as they carried their own food and other necessities and made only strictly limited purchases of Cuban rum, cigars or other local products.
The law exempts those with valid professional interests in Cuba such as journalists, scholars, sports teams and professionals.

Prior to the Cuban revolution in 1959, regattas from Florida to Havana were annual events. After Fidel Castro took power the regattas were suspended until five years ago, when a fleet of 80 sail and motor craft arrived from Sarasota, Florida.
